title: Microjolt econ snapshot — draft
content:
Purpose:
Quick experimental writeup on a class of short, high-frequency interaction patterns we started calling 'microjolts' — sub-second conversational spikes where a user issues multiple very short prompts back-to-back (e.g., autocomplete / rapid clarification). Goal: quantify latency and $/kQ (dollars per 1k queries) tradeoffs for three serving configurations and capture intuitive heuristics to feed into Optimize recommendations.

Status: draft, exploratory. Not yet calibrated on broader customer traces. Data here is from a synthetic microjolt generator (see linked artifacts) that replays a 5-minute session mix with ~1200 interactions (median tokens per request = 12).

Test matrix (configs):
- A: fast-warm: dedicated slot per-session, small kv-cache prewarm (expected lowest p50)
- B: pooled-batch: multiplexed slot sharing, 8-request batching window (aiming for cost savings, adds queue delay)
- C: prefetched-compact: lightweight prefetch + compact quant profile (40% token cost reduction on decode but CPU overhead)

Workload profile (generator):
- Session length: 3-7 turns (microjolt bursts of 3 quick turns)
- Inter-arrival: 200–900ms (exponential jitter)
- Prompt length: 6–30 tokens (median 12)
- Model: rdx-7b-opt (identical model weights across configs)

Key metrics captured:
- p50, p95, p99 latency (ms) end-to-end (ingest -> final chunk out)
- dollar_per_1k_queries (approx cost estimate using token accounting + slot dwell)
- success_rate (no-fallback / OOM)
- observed queuing fraction (time spent queued vs executing)

Results (single-run snapshot, representative):

ASCII table:
+-----------+-------+-------+--------+--------------+------------+
| Config    | p50ms | p95ms | p99ms  | $ / 1k q     | queued %   |
+-----------+-------+-------+--------+--------------+------------+
| A fast-warm | 78   | 142   | 332    | $4.60        | 3%         |
| B pooled-batch | 210 | 480   | 890    | $1.10        | 40%        |
| C prefetched-compact | 120 | 260 | 520  | $0.72        | 18%       |
+-----------+-------+-------+--------+--------------+------------+

Notes on table: these are illustrative for microjolt pattern. A gives best p50 but is ~6.4x more expensive than C and ~4.2x vs B. B drives cost down via batching but incurs substantial queue time (p99 near 900ms). C is middle-ground: meaningful token cost wins with compact quant + prefetch, with p95 around 260ms which may be acceptable for many UI interactions.

Distribution sketch (latency buckets, percent of queries):
- <100ms: A 62% | B 14% | C 38%
- 100-300ms: A 30% | B 32% | C 44%
- 300-700ms: A 6%  | B 38% | C 14%
- >700ms: A 2%  | B 16% | C 4%

Micro-observations / qualitative:
- Queueing dominates the long tail in pooled-batch (B). Microjolt sessions have bursts that are hard to pack into fixed batching windows without hurting p99.
- Prefetch (C) shows a pragmatic win: upfront CPU to compress tokens + small cache hits reduces per-token decode cost and keeps queuing moderate.
- Dedicated warm slots (A) are best where strict UX SLOs matter (e.g., editing assistants), but the spend hit is substantial for workloads with many short sessions.

Heuristics for mapping to Optimize recommendations (rough):
- If p95 target <= 250ms and qps < 50: prefer A (reserved warm) or C with aggressive prefetch.
- If cost sensitivity is high and p95 can be ~300–400ms: B or C preferred; B if highly burst-tolerant UIs (background tasks), C if interactive but willing to accept modest p50 regression.
- Hybrid suggestion: route tail-tolerant traffic to B; route latency-sensitive microjolts to C with prefetch policy enabled. Use dynamic routing by session-intent tag.

Quick experiment plan (next 2 weeks):
1) Run 10 deterministic replays of the same microjolt trace across all configs to get CI on p99.
2) Vary batching window size in B (20ms, 50ms, 100ms) to find knee for p95 vs $/k.
3) Test C with two quant profiles (compact-1, compact-2) to check CPU overhead vs token reduction.
4) Spike the number of simultaneous sessions (x1, x5, x20) to see how A's slot saturation behaves.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Need real customer microjolt traces to validate synthetic generator. Add request to Customer Insights (linked artifact).
- How does client-side multiplexing (multiple user tabs hitting same session) change the queue profile?
- Explore burst-burst detection in Console to auto-upgrade sessions to A for 30s on detection. Feels valuable but needs cost guardrails.

Quick recommendation for product collateral:
- Produce a short 1-pager 'Microjolt playbook' for DX summarizing: scenario definition, recommended config mapping (A/B/C), and a simple decision flow.
- Add a small chart (p95 vs $/k) for inclusion in Optimize UI as a cost-UX slider.

References / links: replay harness + generator in linked artifacts. See JIRA-OPT-977 for batch-window experiments.

End of draft.

-- Priya
